article.title: NFL EDGE Saturday Evening Brief
article.dek: The Bears flipped to Tyson Bagent and the app already prices him, Chicago's moneyline got cheaper for bettors, and the Value lane woke up with a razor-thin plus-EV read on the Chargers getting 7 in Seattle.

items.headline: The Bears are starting Tyson Bagent — and the app already knows
paragraphs: Multiple outlets reported Saturday that Tyson Bagent will start Sunday against the Jets, taking the majority of first-team reps this week and getting the nod over Case Keenum — the same Keenum who just carved up Philadelphia on Monday night. Caleb Williams (hamstring) is still out. Head coach Ben Johnson wouldn't name a starter Friday, but the app's quarterback feed already lists Bagent as Chicago's expected starter.

That matters because the app's Hit Rate card is Chicago's moneyline. The card's model number — about 69 wins in 100 — already prices Bagent, not Keenum. You don't need to guess what the QB flip does to the number. The board did it for you.
items.takeaway: Bagent starts for Chicago on Sunday; the app's quarterback feed already reflects it, so the Hit Rate card's number already prices him in.

items.headline: The injury news, all in one place
paragraphs: Colts receiver Keenan Allen (groin) was downgraded to OUT on Saturday for the London game against Washington — he was limited in practice, then didn't practice Friday. Indianapolis also elevated Nick Westbrook-Ikhine from the practice squad. The Bucs ruled out four against the Packers: Baker Mayfield (thumb, as expected — Jalon Daniels starts), edge Rueben Bain Jr., tight end Ko Kieft, and cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad). Three more Bucs are questionable.

The Saints will be without linebacker Kaden Elliss (calf) and possibly Pete Werner (stinger) against Atlanta, plus edge rushers Carl Granderson and Anfernee Jennings. And the week's Nick Bosa mystery is resolved: San Francisco's final report lists him OUT against Denver, with receiver Mike Evans (ribs) questionable.
items.takeaway: Allen out in London, four Bucs out, the Saints thin at linebacker, and Bosa officially out — the morning's questionable tags mostly resolved the wrong way.

items.headline: The Value lane is back — barely
paragraphs: This morning the Value lane was empty: no offer met the contract. The evening board has one: the Chargers getting 7 points in Seattle at -105 on DraftKings. The model says the Chargers cover about 50.5 times in 100, and at -105 that prices out to +0.31% expected value — the model's plus-EV play, medium confidence.
items.takeaway: Value = Chargers +7 at -105 (DraftKings), the board's only plus-EV read — and a thin one.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Hit Rate: still Chicago, at a better price
paragraphs: The Hit Rate card answers one question: which supported pick looks most likely to win. Tonight it still says Chicago's moneyline — now at -180 on FanDuel, down from -184 this morning. The model gives the Bears about 68.7 wins in 100 with Bagent, and the expected value sits at -0.80%.

That negative number is not a flaw in the card. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate: this lane forgoes value for win probability on purpose. Note the tripwire too — the app's play-through on this card is -185, and the current -180 is on the right side of it. The price improved and stayed playable.
items.takeaway: Chicago remains the most-likely-to-win supported read, now cheaper at -180 and still inside the app's own play-through.

items.headline: Balanced: the middle lane didn't move
paragraphs: Balanced is the middle ground — a strong pick without paying too much, and a good starting point for a new bettor. Tonight it's the same read as this morning: Philadelphia getting 3.5 points at home against the Rams, at -105 on FanDuel. The model says the Eagles cover about 50.5 times in 100, expected value -3.25%, medium confidence, play-through -108.

Nothing about the card changed because nothing about the game did. Balanced isn't supposed to be the plus-EV play — that's the Value lane's job, and tonight the Value lane finally has something to say.
items.takeaway: Eagles +3.5 at -105 is unchanged from this morning — the middle lane held while the other two moved.

items.headline: Value: what +0.31% actually means
paragraphs: Value is always the model's plus-EV play — that is its whole job. Tonight it's the Chargers +7 at -105 on DraftKings: model 50.45%, expected value +0.31%. In plain terms: at this price, the model's math says you'd come out about 31 cents ahead per $100 staked, on average, over a very long run of identical bets.

That is a real edge by the contract's definition — but it is paper-thin. Half a point of model error wipes it out. This is exactly the kind of read where the app's deliberately conservative sizing earns its keep: the lane fired, so it goes on the card, and the stake stays small.
items.takeaway: A +0.31% edge is the model saying 'technically yes' in a whisper — on the card by the rules, sized like the whisper it is.

items.headline: Saturday: Chicago got cheaper, the Value lane refilled
paragraphs: Chicago's moneyline moved from -184 to -180 at FanDuel since the morning board — the same pick costs less than it did at breakfast. DraftKings still shows -185, and the app's own play-through is -185, so the FanDuel number is the better side of the app's line. The Balanced lane didn't budge: Eagles +3.5 at -105, same as this morning.

The real movement story is the Value lane going from empty to occupied: the Chargers +7 at -105 on DraftKings is the board's new plus-EV read. This is the 6:00 p.m. board — anything that moves overnight, or any price your book shows that isn't FanDuel's or DraftKings', won't match these numbers exactly. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator for a bet-or-no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: The moves are in the board — bet your book's number, not the board's; Check prices your actual ticket.

items.headline: Inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff — London goes first
paragraphs: The inactive lists drop about 90 minutes before each kickoff, and tomorrow's first one is the London game: Colts vs Commanders kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET, so inactives land around 8:00 a.m. ET. That's when the questionable tags — and any late downgrades like Allen's — become final.
If a designation flips a game you were eyeing, don't bet the stale number. Open Check, type in the fresh line and price, and get the verdict on the game as it actually is.
items.takeaway: Watch the 90-minute lists starting early for London; Check re-prices anything that flips.

items.headline: Betting term of the day: handle
paragraphs: The splits sites show two numbers: BET is the percentage of tickets (how many bets), HND is the percentage of handle (how much money). When most of the tickets are on one side but most of the money is on the other, that's a disagreement between the public and the bigger, usually sharper money — and that's what a Fade watches for.

Tonight there was nothing to fade: the free splits row is showing a college game, not an NFL one, so there's no verified NFL split to read. The term still matters — when you see tickets and handle pointing opposite ways on a Sunday board, you'll know what you're looking at.
items.takeaway: Tickets count the bets, handle counts the money — a real Fade needs them disagreeing on an NFL game, which tonight they aren't showing.

evidence.fact: Saturday afternoon/evening QB and injury updates: Bears are expected to start QB Tyson Bagent vs the Jets on Sunday — he took the majority of first-team reps this week and gets the nod over Case Keenum, who won Monday night vs Philadelphia (multiple outlets Saturday, via The Athletic's Dan Wiederer and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport; head coach Ben Johnson declined to name a starter Friday). Caleb Williams (hamstring) remains out. Colts WR Keenan Allen (groin) was downgraded to OUT on Saturday for Sunday's London game vs Washington; he was limited in practice and DNP Friday. Buccaneers ruled out four vs the Packers: QB Baker Mayfield (thumb, expected), edge Rueben Bain Jr. (groin/shoulder), TE Ko Kieft, CB Benjamin Morrison (quad); LB SirVocea Dennis, DL Rakeem Nunez-Roches and CB Jacob Parrish questionable. Saints: LB Kaden Elliss (calf) OUT and LB Pete Werner (stinger) questionable vs the Falcons; EDGE Carl Granderson (ankle) and EDGE Anfernee Jennings (knee) OUT. 49ers: DE Nick Bosa officially OUT vs the Broncos (final Friday report), resolving the week's conflicting reports; WR Mike Evans (ribs) questionable.
evidence.interpretation: The Bagent news is the day's biggest development and the app already prices it. Allen's downgrade thins the Colts' receiving corps in London. Bosa officially out removes the week's uncertainty.
evidence.app_guidance: Questionable tags resolve in the inactive lists about 90 minutes before kickoff — watch the list, and use Check to re-price any pick if a designation flips after the board.
